headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Notion AI’s shared workspace content can flow into Roo Code’s filesystem- and network-capable environment.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can surface workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Roo Code can read workspace files and use MCP/networked tools. If Notion content is copied or synced into Roo Code, attacker-controlled text could be treated as instructions. This is not provably blocked, but the bridge is indirect rather than a default raw parser path.
conditions: IF Notion workspace content is copied into Roo Code prompts or files without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF Roo Code is configured to execute instructions from pasted or file-based content, the risk increases.
mitigations: Paste only quoted excerpts, not whole pages.
Add a prompt prefix that treats imported text as untrusted data.
Disable MCP tools for sessions that ingest Notion content.
Review any copied Notion text before sending it to Roo Code.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, and Roo Code has broad filesystem read/write plus broad network egress to configured model APIs and MCP servers. Shared workspace state and user OAuth access create a realistic path for sensitive workspace content to reach external services through Roo Code. The blast radius can include exfiltration of workspace data.
conditions: IF the same workspace content is opened in both tools, Roo Code can read it from disk and transmit it outward.
IF Roo Code is configured with a third-party model API key or MCP server, copied Notion content may leave the workspace.
mitigations: Keep Notion pages containing sensitive data out of the shared VS Code workspace.
Use a separate workspace for Roo Code when handling Notion-derived material.
Remove or disable external model/MCP endpoints for that session.
Redact secrets before copying content from Notion into Roo Code.
Restrict Roo Code to local-only tasks for sensitive projects.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has shared workspace state across instances, while Roo Code can write the filesystem and modify git state with per-step approval. Both agents can act on the same mutable workspace, so concurrent edits can overwrite or conflict. Because Roo Code’s write surface is broad and Notion’s workspace state is shared, the conflict risk is substantial.
conditions: IF both agents edit the same files or workspace pages concurrently, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites files that mirror Notion content, divergence is likely.
mitigations: Assign one agent as the sole writer for each artifact.
Pause Roo Code edits while Notion pages are being updated.
Use git branches or duplicate pages to separate workstreams.
Manually reconcile diffs before committing or publishing.
Turn off automatic file writes for sessions that ingest Notion content.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content, and Roo Code can act on files and git state. If Roo Code consumes Notion output as authoritative, errors or hallucinations can cascade into code changes or commits. The pathway exists in default workflows, but verification can interrupt it.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Notion-generated summaries as source-of-truth, downstream actions may encode errors.
IF Notion output is pasted into Roo Code without verification, the cascade becomes likely.
mitigations: Require a human check before any commit based on Notion output.
Ask Roo Code to verify claims against primary sources.
Keep Notion summaries separate from implementation tasks.
Use explicit citations or links back to source pages.
Block auto-commit workflows for Notion-derived tasks.

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages under Notion workspace permissions, while Roo Code can send data to any configured OpenAI-compatible API and MCP servers. If regulated or residency-bound content from Notion is copied into Roo Code, it may flow to external processors with different retention or residency terms. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated content is copied from Notion into Roo Code and sent to a third-party API, residency/compliance risk materializes.
IF the configured model provider or MCP server has different retention terms than Notion, policy mismatch occurs.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Roo Code prompts.
Use a provider with matching contractual terms.
Disable external API calls for compliance-sensitive sessions.
Document which data classes may move from Notion to Roo Code.
Review retention settings before sharing any workspace content.
